title: Euclidean smooth cutoffs on concentric balls
statement: Use $\mathbf R$ [def-weil-field]. For every integer $m\geq1$, every $c\in\mathbf R^m$, and every pair $0<a<b$ of real numbers, there exists a smooth function $\beta:\mathbf R^m\to\mathbf R$ such that $\beta=1$ on the closed Euclidean ball $\overline B(c,a)$, the closure of $\{x:\beta(x)\ne0\}$ is $\overline B(c,b)$, and this closure is compact.
